The Linux hint (free -h, the Mem line) has not been run this month and its output is not captured.
stands: GB is short for gigabyte, the unit memory is counted in.
why: One number decides whether a model runs at all. The app found Priya's number for her, and it chose well. One day it'll choose badly, and the sticky note is how you check.
mnem: Memory is the room, not the speed.

steps.text: Find your number: how much **memory** your machine has, in GB. (Memory is the space your laptop works in. Whatever it's doing right now has to be in there.) On a Mac: Apple menu, About This Mac, the line that says Memory.
steps.hint: It might say RAM instead. Same thing. On Linux you already know, and I know you know (`free -h`, the Mem line).

doIt.explain: I'll give you the exact clicks for your machine, one at a time.

check.question: Found it? Write it on a sticky note and put it on the lid.
check.rubric: The learner says they have found the Memory or RAM line. No number is needed yet.

steps.text: Type the number from your sticky note. I'll check it against what the machine says.
steps.hint: Just the number, in GB. If you see two numbers, use the bigger one.

doIt.explain: I'll read the number from the machine myself and show you exactly what I ran.

onFail.say: You typed {typed} GB and the machine says {measured} GB. Did you read the drive by mistake? The drive is the warehouse. Memory is the room.

steps.text: Now the test. For each of these, say fits or doesn't fit: a 2 GB **model file**, a 5 GB one, a 20 GB one. (The model file is the single file a model is downloaded as: the whole of the clever part, in one lump.)
steps.hint: My **rule of thumb**: under about three quarters of your number, fine. Over it, a squeeze. Bigger than the number, no.

doIt.explain: I'll work it through with your number, one file at a time.

check.question: A 2 GB file, a 5 GB file, a 20 GB file: fits or doesn't fit?
check.rubric: Judge against the measured number N. A file fits if it is no bigger than N, and is a squeeze if it is over three quarters of N. On 16 GB: fits, fits, no. On 32 GB: fits, fits, fits. On 8 GB: fits, fits, no.

onFail.say: Close. A 20 GB file needs 20 GB of room, and the drive doesn't count. The choir doesn't sing in the warehouse.

recap: Memory is the room a model has to fit in, whole, before it can speak. Your sticky-note number.
The model file is one file holding the whole model. Fits in memory or it does not run.
Three quarters of your number is comfortable; over it is a squeeze; over the number is no.
